**Acknowledgements, from GC Wealth Project Director Salvatore Morelli**

The project was launched in June 2023 after approximately five years of development. This version of the data warehouse is launched in the Fall 2024. Many individuals contributed to varying degrees, during multiple stages, and to different sections of the project. First, the project would not exist without the continuous, reliable, and professional support of the Stone Center, including its director Janet Gornick, and the staff, Carolyn Fisher, Mei-Ling Israel, Jennifer Kitses, Veronica Ordaz, and Saraya McPherson. I also acknowledge the support from the Law Department of the University of Roma Tre, including the current director Antonio Carratta, as well as the admin staff Giuseppina Santilli and Federico Melograno. The communication support from Ylenia Sina is also acknowledged.

A number of people provided valuable feedback on a number of aspects during the early stages of the project. I particular, I am grateful to  Facundo Alvaredo, Charlotte Bartels, Yonatan Berman, Miles Corak, Philipp Erfurth, Josep Espasa Reig, Giacomo Gabbuti, Janet Gornick, Demetrio Guzzardi, Elena Granaglia, Joe Hasell, Roberto Iacono,  Rama Dasi Mariani, Branko Milanovic, Teresa Munzi, Jorg Neugschwender, Brian Nolan, Juan Palomino, Piotr Paradowski, Alberto Pozzolo, Antonio Scialà, and Philippe Van Kerm. 

Regarding the Wealth Topography database, I acknowledge the instrumental initial contribution by Gonçalo Costa in conceptualizing the database and initiating the first systematic data-gathering effort. Giacomo Rella then oversaw the development of the Wealth Topography database under its current form. Max Longmuir followed in taking the lead. Both carried out various essential tasks, including conceptualization, designing the current data architecture, the national accounting mapping, the automation of data gathering, and the design of the detailed metadata complementing the database. I would also like to thank Ana Rojas Silvero for providing valuable assistance in gathering and classifying raw sources on household balance sheets. My thanks also go to Marco Ranaldi, Yaoqi Lin, and Pranabes Probeshika Dutta for their support with the initial data gathering.

The initial collaborative work of Frincasco Di Biase and Ercio Muñoz, proved instrumental in gathering the available data series for the Wealth Inequality section. Franziska Disslbacher took an oversight role of the Wealth Inequality database in 2022 and part of 2023, making possible a first database automation process. 

In 2023 Matteo Targa took over Franziska’s role and identified methods to automatically detect problems within the data series. Furthermore, together with Ignacio and Franziska, Matteo enabled the estimation of wealth inequality trends series using cross-national survey databases.  Finally, Matteo has also taken the lead in the management, update, expansion, and streamlining process of the inequality trends database. The development of methodological tables to supplement the inequality trends series was carried out by me, with meticulous assistance from Francesco Di Biase, Franziska Disslbacher, and Matteo Targa throughout the process, which was instrumental in deriving the final tables in their current form. I am  also very grateful to Tony Shorrocks for sharing Credit Suisse data.

Adam Rego Johnson played a pivotal role in creating compilation standards and manuals, as well as providing invaluable work in editing, proofreading, and classifying the tables. He also played a fundamental role in systematizing and classifying references, including within the Digital Library of Research on Wealth Inequality and the Data Sources Library. The initial work conducted by Carolyn Fisher, Ian Haberman, Twisha Asher, and subsequent contributions by Franziska Disslbacher, were important in finalizing the conceptual structure of the methodological tables, as well as providing content for specific sources. 

Regarding the Taxes on Wealth section, I would like to acknowledge the dedicated work of Twisha Asher, who collected and classified estate, inheritance, and gift (EIG) tax policy parameters and researched corporate reports, official statistics, tax legislation documents, and research papers. She also played a crucial role in supporting the conceptualization and documentation of the current structure of the Taxes on Wealth database. I would also like to acknowledge important contributions by Manuel Schechtl, who assumed the oversight role on the development of the Taxes on Wealth database from Dec 2022 through July 2024. Jointly with Twisha Asher and Ignacio Flores, Manuel Schechtl also helped clarify the code to assemble the database and streamline the data collection process. Twisha Asher, alongside with Manuel Schechtl, also supervised a number of excellent research assistants who worked on different aspects of the project: Mei Li, Nolan Lyons, Yue Pan, Alex Parton, Sarah Russo, Jack Shea, and Tsu Zhu. Francesca Subioli and Luca Giangregorio joined Manuel’s work in supervising the development of the tax section in early and late 2023, respectively. Both have identified bottlenecks in the coding structure, fully restructured the Taxes on Wealth database using a new and more effective architecture, and planned part of the development of future database expansion. Moreover, they supervised the excellent research assistance of Martino Kuntze, Ali Jehanzaib, and Ghulam Shabir who helped systematize the information contained in relevant sources and helped debug the data entry process for the Taxes on Wealth section. Ignacio Flores played a crucial role in overseeing the overall architecture of the data warehouse. His work allowed for the integration of various components, resulting in a cohesive and well-structured data warehouse.

Special thanks to Mark Sheppard who helped to create the GC Wealth Project logo, the thumbnails, and visual banners for the website in the months leading up to the launch of the website. The project also relied on the expertise of external consultants. Toni Johnson provided invaluable support as director of communication in the early phase of the project. We extend thanks to Marcelo Agudo for his editing work, and to Robert Breen for his assistance with Tableau. We would like to acknowledge Rodica Ceslov and Connie Colvin for their support as project managers during earlier, separate phases of the project. Finally, we are grateful to the Lovelytics team for their assistance in the initial design of the Tableau dashboard and for their contribution to the website development.
